Fair Division: Lone Divider

AlgorithmsGraph TheoryLogic
Game: One player cuts the goods; everyone else picks a piece they would accept.
How to play: Click cells to mark a chooser's acceptable pieces, then press Solve to match them.

Look for the math

With one divider and several choosers, a careful rule makes everyone feel fairly treated.

The divider's advantage

The divider cuts n pieces that they consider equally valuable, so any piece is fair to them. Every chooser marks the pieces they would accept. A piece nobody marks goes straight to the divider. The rest must be matched one-to-one to the choosers who accept them — an instance of the matching problem in graph theory.

When matching fails

If two choosers accept only the same piece, no perfect matching exists and a partial division must be followed by another round among the remaining players. The logic test checks 500 random preference tables: every assigned piece is acceptable, no chooser gets two pieces, and all pieces are accounted for.

For two players this becomes the famous rule: one cuts, the other chooses first.
